title: Cached playback manifests with signed URLs
name: Playback manifest service

questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code chooses the lifetime of cached manifests? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
A user's subscription is cancelled while a manifest for a video is cached. What happens when that user requests the manifest again?
choices: They receive the cached manifest until it expires
assertCanWatch runs first and throws, so the cached manifest is not served
The cache entry is removed and rebuilt for the user
They receive the manifest but segment requests fail

questions.prompt: Many viewers request a newly released video at the same moment, none of them hitting a cache entry. What does the code do?
choices: Only one request builds the manifest; the others wait
Each request that misses builds and caches its own manifest; the result is equivalent but the catalog and signer are called redundantly
The cache refuses puts for a key being built

questions.prompt: What does ManifestCache.get do when it finds an entry whose expiry has passed?
choices: Returns the entry and refreshes its expiry
Returns an empty Optional and leaves the entry in place
Removes that specific entry and returns an empty Optional
